subject: English
passage: "Boy Life on the Prairie" is an 1899 work by Hamlin Garland. In the work, the narrator explains that he prefers the prairie of his childhood to other landscapes he has encountered: ______
prompt: Which quotation from "Boy Life on the Prairie" most effectively illustrates this claim?

choices.A: "There is always some new shade of grass, some shift of cloud, some turn of light worth pausing to observe."
choices.B: "A wide creek curves through the valley just east of the homestead, and its banks, fringed with cottonwoods and tall rushes, descend softly toward meadows that shimmer in the summer wind."
choices.C: "I have wandered widely across this continent and been stirred by much that I have seen, but nothing has stirred me so deeply as the rolling grasslands of the prairie where I was a boy."
choices.D: "There is a steady satisfaction in learning the moods of any country one chooses to call one's own."

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most effectively illustrates the claim that the narrator prefers the prairie of his childhood to other landscapes he has encountered. In the quotation, the narrator acknowledges having traveled widely and been moved by many sights, but states that nothing has stirred him as deeply as the prairie grasslands of his boyhood — a direct comparative preference for his home landscape over other places he has seen.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. Although the quotation describes a landscape of creeks, cottonwoods, and meadows in appealing terms, it does not specify that this landscape is the prairie of the narrator's childhood, nor does it express any preference for it over other places the narrator has visited.
